lines.text: Guruji, tell me the battle story again!
Then listen, Ganga, and carve every word. It is the story of our king, Pulakeshin.
In the north ruled Harsha, the mightiest emperor of his time, with a sea of war elephants.
And he wanted the south as well.
But at the Narmada river, a young king was waiting.
Harsha's elephants charged into the river, and one by one, they fell.
And when Harsha saw his elephants fall, his harsha melted away.
Harsha means joy! He lost his joy!
From that day, Pulakeshin was called the Lord of the South.
Even a traveller from China, Xuanzang, wrote that Harsha could never defeat his soldiers.
Now carve my name at the end. Ravikirti, as famous as Kalidasa.
